messages:
Jane (Acct): Hi all — customer running Redwood in an air-gapped colo. App calls https://inference.redwood.internal but fails from the app host. Seeing TLS errors and occasional 407 from the corporate proxy. Can we triage?

Alex K: Thanks. Can you paste the app error and a quick curl -v from the same host?

Jane (Acct): App log: "rpc: Post \"https://inference.redwood.internal/v1/generate\": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"

And curl without proxy configured:
```
$ curl -v https://inference.redwood.internal/v1/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://inference.redwood.internal/v1/health
*   Trying 10.11.12.13...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to inference.redwood.internal (10.11.12.13) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* Server certificate: CN=corp-proxy.local
* ALPN, server accepted to use http/1.1
* SSL: certificate subject name (corp-proxy.local) does not match target host name 'inference.redwood.internal'
* Closing connection 0
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS header, Certificate Status (22):
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS alert, Server hello (2): fatal, description = unexpected_message
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL: certificate subject name (corp-proxy.local) does not match target host name 'inference.redwood.internal'
```

Jane (Acct): When I add HTTP_PROXY env we see 407: Proxy Authentication Required. The PAC file points at corpproxy.corp:3128.

Sanjay P: Looks like the proxy is doing TLS interception (re-signing with corp-proxy.local). Two immediate vectors: 1) proxy is terminating TLS (MITM) breaking hostname/pinning, 2) proxy denies unauthenticated CONNECT (407).

Maya I: Can you run an openssl test to confirm server_name and cert chain?

Jane (Acct): Running openssl gave: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.11.12.13:443 -servername inference.redwood.internal -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = corp-proxy.local
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=corp-proxy.local
   i:/CN=Corp Internal CA
---
No client certificate CA names sent
---
SSL handshake has read 2783 bytes and written 508 bytes
---

```

Jane (Acct): So yeah, proxy is presenting corp cert. The app uses certificate pinning so rejects it.

Alex K: Two paths: ask proxy team to enable TLS passthrough for inference hosts (CONNECT tunnel without MITM) OR add the corp CA to the app/trusted store (if allowed). But for short term, confirm whether proxy can allow CONNECT tunneling for inference.redwood.internal and whether firewall allowlist has our outbound IP blocks.

Ryan O: Also ensure DNS is not being rewritten by the proxy/firewall. If they rewrite to an internal IP for inspection, SNI tests will still present corp cert. Please share PAC contents and firewall egress rules if possible.

Jane (Acct): PAC excerpt: 
```
function FindProxyForURL(url, host) {
  if (dnsDomainIs(host, ".internal") ) return "PROXY corpproxy.corp:3128";
  return "DIRECT";
}
```

Jane (Acct): Firewall egress currently allows destinations by FQDN pattern ".redwood.internal" but they only allow CONNECT to port 443 if proxy auth present. They block raw outbound to our public IP ranges except a small list (we asked for more).

Sanjay P: Ok reproduce checklist we usually follow: 
1) From host: curl -v --proxy "http://corpuser:xxxx@corpproxy.corp:3128" https://inference.redwood.internal/v1/health 
2) curl -v --noproxy inference.redwood.internal https://inference.redwood.internal/v1/health (to see direct path) 
3) openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername inference.redwood.internal | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates 
4) tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 443 to confirm SYN dest IP and check if TLS bytes are actually from proxy

Jane (Acct): Ran step 1 (with creds) and got 200 OK. Step 2 fails (no direct route). Step 3 shows corp-proxy cert. Step 4 shows traffic to proxy IP 10.1.2.2 not to our expected public IPs.

Maya I: That confirms MITM. For customers in air-gapped/managed networks we recommend one of: 
- Allow outbound CONNECT (443) to our hostnames/IP ranges with TLS passthrough (preferred)
- If TLS inspection is required, add the inspection CA to the application keystore or the OS CA bundle used by the Redwood client.
- If proxy requires auth and app can't provide it, configure a proxy credential mapping (service account) or use an egress gateway that does auth on behalf of services.

Alex K: For squid specifically, the proxy team can add an ACL to allow TLS passthrough for our hosts: 
```
acl redwood_ssl ssl::server_name .redwood.internal
http_access allow redwood_ssl
# ensure tls_outgoing_options allow CONNECT to 443 for that acl
```
Or to force tunnel and not MITM:
```
tls_outgoing_options cafile /etc/squid/certs/ca-bundle.crt 
# and disable ssl_bump for acl redwood_ssl
```

Jane (Acct): We pushed to proxy team. They said they cannot disable inspection globally but can add exceptions per-host. They'll try passthrough for inference.redwood.internal and also add our documented IP ranges. What IPs should they allow?

Sanjay P: We publish our egress ranges in the support doc, but for temporary testing you can allow the documentation test blocks: 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/24 (RFC5737 ranges we asked them to permit for this colo). Eventually they'll need the full list from our account portal.

Ryan O: Also ensure SNI passthrough is preserved; some L7 load balancers will terminate SNI unless configured for TCP mode. Ask for TCP/CONNECT passthrough.

Jane (Acct): Proxy team applied a rule to bypass MITM for inference.redwood.internal and allowed the 198.51.100.0/24 block. I re-ran curl without proxy env and it works: 
```
$ curl -v https://inference.redwood.internal/v1/health
* Connected to inference.redwood.internal (198.51.100.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS header, Certificate Status (22):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Finished (20)
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* Server certificate: CN=inference.redwood.internal
* Server certificate: subject=CN=inference.redwood.internal
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: inference.redwood.internal
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK

```

Jane (Acct): App still failed initially because the app container had an old CA bundle. Once we updated the container's trusted roots (added corp proxy CA because they still inspect some other hosts) and kept passthrough for the inference host, everything green now.

Alex K: Great. Follow-up actions: 
- Customer: keep the proxy exception for our hostname and request the full IP list from your account page to add to firewall egress allowlist.
- Support: add note to ticket about recommend TLS passthrough as default for pinned/pinned-key apps.
- Infra: consider adding a small KB about proxy/TLS inspection for air-gapped deployments.

support-bot: Ticket #SUP-8912 created and linked to this thread.

Jane (Acct): Thanks everyone — I'll close once customer confirms in 24h. :white_check_mark:
